definitions.explanation: The quality of being bitter in taste. Used when discussing flavors in food, drink, and cooking. One of the five basic tastes.

examples.japanese: このコーヒーは{苦味|にがみ}が{強|つよ}い。
examples.english: This coffee has a strong bitterness.

examples.japanese: ゴーヤの{苦味|にがみ}が{苦手|にがて}な{人|ひと}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many people dislike the bitterness of bitter melon.

examples.japanese: {大人|おとな}になるにつれて、{苦味|にがみ}のある{食|た}べ{物|もの}を{好|この}むようになる{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いらしい。
examples.english: Apparently, many people come to enjoy bitter-tasting foods as they grow older.

notes:
USAGE:
{苦味|にがみ} refers specifically to the bitter component of a flavor. It is one of the five basic tastes alongside {甘味|あまみ} (sweetness), {酸味|さんみ} (sourness), {塩味|しおみ} (saltiness), and {旨味|うまみ} (umami).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {苦味|にがみ}が{強|つよ}い (strongly bitter)
- {苦味|にがみ}を{感|かん}じる (taste bitterness)
- {苦味|にがみ}が{効|き}いている (the bitterness comes through)
- {苦味|にがみ}{成分|せいぶん} (bitter component)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {苦|にが}さ: bitterness (general quality, can be figurative — bitterness of experience)
- {渋味|しぶみ}: astringency (puckering taste, as in unripe persimmon or strong tea)
- {酸味|さんみ}: sourness, acidity (another taste quality)
